title: 2026 Minnesota gubernatorial election
description: Minnesota will elect its next governor in 2026, with the governor serving as chief executive of the state and overseeing the budget, agencies, and implementation of state law. The race is likely to center on taxes, education, public safety, abortion, and state spending, reflecting broader partisan debates in Minnesota. Ballotpedia says general-election candidates will be added after the primaries, and the Minnesota Secretary of State is the official source for candidate filings and election information. Tim Walz is the incumbent governor, but available sources here do not establish that he is on the 2026 ballot.
polling_note: No public polling found for this race in the last 90 days as of 2026-05-17.

candidates.name: Tim Walz
candidates.summary: Tim Walz is Minnesota’s 41st governor and a former educator and Army National Guard veteran. He was first elected governor in 2018 and won re-election in 2022; the Minnesota governor’s office says he later announced he would not seek a third term.

summary_sources.title: Governor Walz Statement Announcing He Will Not Seek Reelection

career_history.title: Teacher and football coach
career_history.description: Worked in education before entering full-time politics.

candidates.donor_summary: OpenSecrets and the FEC show Tim Walz’s federal campaign committees raised about $113,150.64 in the 2017–2018 cycle, with most receipts coming from other committees ($80,650) rather than individual donors. OpenSecrets’ profile page is available, but the page text available here does not expose a clean top-industries list; the best public finance page to review is the FEC candidate overview, with state-level disclosure also available through Minnesota’s campaign finance board and FollowTheMoney.

candidates.voting_summary: Tim Walz is an incumbent governor, not a legislator, so there is no legislative voting record to report for the 2026 governor race. His public governing record is instead as Minnesota governor since 2019, and his official state bio confirms he was first elected governor in 2018 and re-elected in 2022.

Healthcare.stance: Walz has proposed a major overhaul of Minnesota’s human services and Medicaid administration, including moving more functions to the state level and ending the use of managed care organizations. He says the changes are intended to modernize systems, improve transparency, and reduce fraud.

sources.title: Governor Walz Announces Proposal to Transform Minnesota’s Human Services System
Walz unveils plan to 'transform' Minnesota's human services system

Economy.stance: Walz’s 2026 supplemental budget proposal focuses on lowering costs for middle-class families, including child care refunds, affordable housing, and sales tax relief, while also funding workforce preparation and targeted tax measures affecting large tech firms. He describes the plan as a balanced approach to growth and affordability.

sources.title: Governor Walz Proposes Balanced Budget to Lower Costs, Make Big Tech Pay Their Fair Share, and Respond to Operation Metro Surge
GOVERNOR WALZ’S 2026 SUPPLEMENTAL BUDGET (One Pager)

Climate/Energy.stance: Walz supports aggressive climate action and a transition to clean energy. As governor, he signed Minnesota’s 100% clean electricity law for 2040 and issued an executive order to streamline environmental permitting for clean-energy projects.

sources.title: Governor Walz Signs Bill Moving Minnesota to 100 Percent Clean Electricity by 2040
Governor Walz Issues Executive Order Reforming Environmental Permitting

Abortion & Reproductive Health.stance: Walz supports abortion access and reproductive freedom. In 2023 he signed the Protect Reproductive Options Act, which codified reproductive freedom into Minnesota law and protected abortion and contraception access.

sources.title: Governor Walz Signs Reproductive Freedom into Law - PRO Act
Governor Walz signs broad abortion rights bill into law

Immigration.stance: Walz has backed more permissive immigration policies in Minnesota, including expanding driver’s license access to residents regardless of immigration status. He has also defended Minnesota’s approach to immigrant communities and said he supports broader immigration reform rather than mass deportations.

sources.title: Governor Walz Signs Bill Expanding Access to Driver's Licenses
Walz says federal immigration crackdown in Minnesota could end within days

Firearms & Second Amendment.stance: Walz supports a broad gun-violence-prevention agenda that includes universal background checks, an assault-weapons ban, a high-capacity magazine ban, ghost-gun restrictions, safe-storage requirements, and stronger reporting and enforcement measures. He has also backed giving local governments more flexibility by revisiting state preemption rules.

sources.title: Governor Walz Announces Comprehensive Gun Violence Prevention Package
Gun Violence Prevention Package - Fact Sheet

Tech & AI.stance: Walz supports stronger AI regulation, including signing a Minnesota law banning AI nudification technology that creates non-consensual nude images. The law includes enforcement provisions and penalties for violations.

sources.title: Governor Walz Signs Bills
Minnesota Gov. Walz signs first-of-its-kind law to stop AI being used for CSAM

Election Policy.stance: Walz supported and signed Minnesota voting-access legislation that expanded automatic voter registration, allowed 16- and 17-year-olds to pre-register, and created a permanent absentee voting system. The changes were designed to make voting easier for eligible Minnesota voters.

Local Issues.stance: Walz has emphasized state support for local communities through initiatives such as Shop Local Minnesota and through efforts to modernize human services delivery. His stated goal is to strengthen local businesses and improve how residents access services.

Gov. Walz to announce changes to Minnesota's human services system

Civil Rights & Equality.stance: Walz has publicly supported civil-rights protections and LGBTQ+ equality as governor. His office has issued proclamations recognizing events such as Transgender Day of Visibility, and he has defended nondiscrimination policies in public remarks.

Education.stance: Walz supports the Due North Education Plan, which aims to reform school finance, expand opportunities in Greater Minnesota, strengthen the teaching workforce, and add student supports such as mental health services and family engagement. The plan also emphasizes recovery from COVID-19 learning disruptions and equitable standards.

candidates.summary: Jeff Johnson is a Minnesota Republican politician who served in the Minnesota House of Representatives from 2001 to 2007 and on the Hennepin County Board from 2009 to 2021. He was the Republican nominee for governor in 2014 and 2018 and announced another gubernatorial campaign in 2025.

His campaign website says he is a public policy graduate, holds a Master of Public Policy degree, and previously worked as a legislative assistant in the Minnesota Senate; Ballotpedia also lists retail work among his career experience.

He also backs universal childcare and tax policies such as a wealth tax and higher rates on very high incomes.

flags.concern: The donor summary for Tim Walz cites a 2017–2018 federal campaign cycle ($113,150.64) but the profile is dated 2026-05-17. For an incumbent governor running in 2026, this federal-era data is stale and not directly relevant to a state gubernatorial campaign. State-level finance data would be more current and appropriate, though the profile does correctly point to the Minnesota Campaign Finance Board as the authoritative source.
flags.suggestion: Consider prioritizing the most recent state-level fundraising data from the Minnesota Campaign Finance Board rather than leading with obsolete federal House campaign data from nearly a decade prior.

flags.concern: The polling section includes two entries, but the second (SurveyUSA, 2026-02-05) has no sample size, no percentages for the 'Unnamed Republican opponents' matchup, and appears incomplete. The polling_note field states 'No public polling found for this race in the last 90 days as of 2026-05-17,' yet the February 5 entry would fall outside that 90-day window from May 17. The incomplete matchup data may indicate a failed scrape or a placeholder entry.
flags.suggestion: Either complete the February 5 SurveyUSA entry with sample size and percentages, or remove it if the data could not be reliably retrieved. Clarify in the source URL or entry whether this was an incomplete data extraction.

flags.concern: Kobey Layne's education entry lists 'Unknown institution' for his Master of Public Policy degree. The campaign website (cited source) states he is 'a public policy graduate' with an MPP, but the issuing institution is not specified in the available source text. This is not a factual error but an incomplete data extraction.
flags.suggestion: If the institution cannot be retrieved from the campaign website, consider noting in the education field that the institution is not publicly disclosed or verifiable from available sources, rather than listing 'Unknown institution.'

flags.concern: Jeff Johnson's donor summary references $866,000 cash on hand from 2014 and other older fundraising data. For a 2026 governor race, this data is now over 10 years old and does not reflect current 2025–2026 fundraising. While the profile correctly points to the Minnesota Campaign Finance Board as the authoritative current source, the accessible page text 'does not show receipts, donor industries, or large contributions,' suggesting either the board's page did not load completely or current 2026 data is not yet fully available.
flags.suggestion: Update or supplement with the most recent available 2025–2026 data once the Minnesota Campaign Finance Board filings are complete. Note the data gap explicitly if 2026 filings have not yet been made public.

flags.concern: The firearms stance for Jeff Johnson describes his proposal as an 'optional Minnesota Citizens Enhanced Protection Act' framed as 'a training and preparedness measure.' The phrase 'optional...Enhanced Protection Act' is somewhat vague. The source (ontheissues.org) should be spot-checked to confirm whether Johnson explicitly labeled this proposal as 'optional' or whether the description originated in the profile.
flags.suggestion: Verify against the source URL whether 'optional' is Johnson's language or an interpretive addition by the profile compiler. If his actual position differs, adjust the stance description accordingly.

reviews.summary: This is a well-sourced and professionally compiled profile of the 2026 Minnesota gubernatorial race. The profile demonstrates strong research across three major candidates with appropriate differentiation between candidates with extensive legislative/executive records (Walz) versus newer or less-established candidates (Layne). Sourcing is robust: Tim Walz's issue positions are backed by official press releases and news coverage from reputable outlets; Jeff Johnson's positions cite recent announcements and policy repositories; Kobey Layne's stances are drawn directly from his official campaign website. Candidate backgrounds are internally consistent with cited sources, and the distinction between "no public position found" (a legitimate absence) and substantive positions is properly maintained. The profile appropriately documents Tim Walz's decision not to seek reelection while noting polling still includes him. Language remains neutral across partisan divides, with stance descriptions avoiding loaded terminology. Minor areas for improvement noted below do not substantially undermine profile quality.

flags.concern: The profile notes that Tim Walz announced he would not seek a third term. My training data suggests he has previously expressed interest in various political paths, and while this statement is backed by the provided URL, a human reviewer should confirm this specific 'not seeking re-election' status remains the current official stance as of mid-2026.
flags.suggestion: Verify the status of the governor's 2026 ballot filing or withdrawal declaration at the Minnesota Secretary of State’s official portal.

flags.concern: The poll lists a 2026-01-30 matchup between Tim Walz and Jeff Johnson. Given the conflicting information regarding Governor Walz's candidacy, this poll should be treated as a snapshot of hypothetical or early-cycle data.

The education section lists the years for degrees as 'null'. While accurate to the provided sources, a quick check could verify if those dates are retrievable from university directories for better completeness.
flags.suggestion: If available, add graduation years for the J.D. and B.A. programs to improve detail.

reviews.summary: This profile is exceptionally well-structured and demonstrates high-quality research practices. The candidate backgrounds are detailed and consistently supported by official government links and reputable news sources. The summary of policy positions is balanced, and the profile correctly identifies where public information is absent (noting low confidence in those areas) rather than attempting to fabricate stances. The distinction between incumbent status, past legislative history, and current campaign platforms is clearly maintained throughout.

Strong, well-sourced profile with consistent internal sourcing across all candidates. Tim Walz’s section is particularly robust, with high-confidence issue stances backed by official Minnesota government press releases and credible news outlets. Jeff Johnson and Kobey Layne sections are also well-documented using campaign websites, Ballotpedia, and news coverage. Neutral language is maintained throughout with no partisan framing or loaded terminology. Gaps (e.g., “No public position found”) are appropriately noted after apparent good-faith searches.
